primary_claim: Frontier models prompted to imitate a specific weaker predecessor model shift into a generic weaker-capability error pattern but do not reproduce that predecessor's specific per-question mistake fingerprint (e.g. changing only the named predecessor between two similar-capability models like GPT-4o and Sonnet 4 leaves the simulator's chosen wrong answer unchanged 93-97% of the time); targeted single-forward-pass sandbagging to a specific weaker identity is thus largely a null result, though prompting the successor to first reason latently (out-of-context) about the predecessor's likely errors measurably improves imitation, and giving the predecessor visible chain-of-thought reasoning is an effective mitigant against being imitated.

effect.metric: paired treatment effect: predecessor-wrong-letter match rate under imitation prompt vs baseline (GSM-MC, GPT 5.4 imitating GPT-4o)
effect.value: matches 24/105 predecessor-wrong items at baseline vs 52/105 when prompted to predict the predecessor's errors first; label-swap between similar-capability predecessors changes the simulator's chosen answer only 3.4-6.6% of the time

stated_future_work: explore other domains where reasoning yields smaller or less sequential gains, to map where the chain-of-thought protection against imitation holds and where it thins
investigate whether requiring predecessors to reason heavily about oversight decisions could shift their answer distribution beyond what a successor could latently imitate
chase the 'modelling the overseer' concern further: whether a successor can learn to predict a weaker evaluator's judgments rather than imitate its identity
limitations_stated: ground-truth judgments (~200 per predecessor) were not manually audited
GPT-4o is likely the best-case predecessor for imitation given how publicised its prompts/responses are, so the identity-null result should only harden on less-known predecessors
some models (e.g. Opus) refuse to simulate specific predecessors directly, making imitation capacity hard to measure via that channel even though behavioral capacity is present
results measure error-imitation rather than actual oversight manipulation, so implications for modelling an overseer are only directional
quote: Successors tested can be pushed toward replicating answers from prior models whose outputs were plausibly in their training distribution. However, the broader result is not impersonation of a specific model, but a capability tier.
